q: 1. The unit of payment for fixing of glass panes or cleaning is in
explain: Glass panes are discrete, countable items, so their fixing or cleaning is paid for on a per-number (piece) basis.

q: 2. The volume of cement in one bag is
explain: Based on a 50kg bag and 1440 kg/m3 density, the volume is approximately 0.0347 cubic meters (often rounded to 0.035).

q: 3. In the estimation of plastering surface the deductions are not made for
explain: Ends of structural members and very small openings are not deducted from total plastering area measurements.

q: 4. In the case of roof truss made of steel, rivets, bolts, nuts etc. normally account for
explain: An additional 5% weight is usually added to the main steel sections to account for connections like rivets and bolts.

q: 5. The item of steel works which is measured is sq. m is
explain: Steel items like collapsible gates, rolling shutters, and ventilators/glazing are all flat, area-covering fabricated items, and hence all are measured in square metres.

q: 6. For the construction of buildings, the subheads of the estimate are
options: Brickwork Flooring, Wood work, Steel work
explain: A building estimate is broken into multiple subheads covering all major trades — earthwork, concrete, brick, stone, roofing, flooring, woodwork, steelwork, etc.

q: 7. The thickness of beam/slab is taken to nearest
explain: As a standard estimating precision, beam/slab thickness is recorded correct to the nearest 5 mm.

q: 8. The amount provisioned for tools and plants on Earthwork excavation item in norms for rate analysis is:
explain: In standard rate analysis norms, tools and plant (T&P) provision for earthwork excavation is taken as 3% of the labour cost component.

q: 9. The unit of measurement of turfing in embankment is called
explain: Turfing (laying grass sod on embankment slopes) is a surface-covering activity, so it is measured by area, square metres.

q: 10. The unit of measurement of site clearance in irrigation canal is
explain: Site clearance for a canal (removing vegetation, debris over the alignment area) is measured by area, in square metres.

q: 11. Indicating works left in excavated trenches to facilitate the measurement of borrow pints are known as
explain: Tell-tale marks/pegs are left in excavated trenches or borrow pits as reference indicators to help verify and measure the quantity of earthwork excavated.

q: 12. The areas of a sloping surface of a protective embankment of mean height d, side slopes S:1 and length L is
explain: The sloping surface area of an embankment is the slope length (which is d√(1+s²), from Pythagoras on horizontal run sd and vertical rise d) multiplied by the embankment length L, giving L·d√(1+s²).

q: 13. A layer of dry bricks put below the foundation concrete, in the case of soft soils, is called
explain: Soling is a layer of dry bricks (or stones) placed below the foundation concrete on soft soils to provide a firm, well-distributed bearing surface.

q: 14. The quantity of partition walls and honey-comb walls are worked out in
explain: Thin partition and honeycomb (jali) walls are treated as area-based masonry items and are measured in square metres.

q: 15. The weight of water per cubic foot is
explain: Water has a density of 1000 kg/m3; converting to cubic feet (1 cu ft = 0.02832 m3) gives a weight of about 28.3 kgf per cubic foot.

q: 16. In case of steel rolling shutter, for the estimation of painted area, the plain area is multiplied by
explain: For rolling shutters, the area is calculated as the size of the opening multiplied by 1.10 to 1.25 (1 1/4) to account for corrugations and overlaps, depending on the specific code used.

q: 17. The volume of coarse aggregate required to make 100 m3 of 1:2:4 concrete is
explain: Using the dry volume factor of 1.54 and the coarse aggregate ratio (4/7) in a 1:2:4 mix, the coarse aggregate quantity for 100 m3 of concrete works out to 88 m3.

q: 18. To account for the corrugation, the plain area of the semi-corrugated asbestos sheet is increased by (for white washing)
explain: Semi-corrugated sheets have fewer curves than fully corrugated sheets, so the standard increase factor is lower, typically 10%.

q: 19. The quantity for expansion joint in building is worked out in
explain: An expansion joint is a narrow, continuous gap running along a line in the structure, so its quantity is worked out by its running length, in metres.

q: 20. The quantity of partition walls and honey-comb walls are worked out in
explain: Being thin walls, partition and honeycomb walls are measured in square meters (area) rather than volume.

q: 21. The unit of measurement of earth in filling
explain: Earth filling is a bulk, volumetric item, so it is measured in cubic metres.

q: 22. The area of the segmental portion of an arch with span, l and rise r is approximately given by
explain: The approximate area of a parabolic segment or a shallow arch is calculated using the formula (2/3) × span × rise.

q: 23. The unit of measurement of 75 mm thick PCC is
explain: Once the thickness (75 mm) is fixed and specified, a PCC layer is measured on an area basis, in square metres.

q: 24. Which of the following is not a common size of reinforcement bars?
explain: While 32mm exists, in standard residential and common civil works, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, and 25mm are the most 'common' sizes used, whereas 32mm is reserved for heavy industrial/bridge works.

q: 25. The unit measurement of RCC works in shelves of jail (thickness and type specified) is
explain: With thickness and type specified, thin RCC shelf slabs are measured on an area basis, in square metres.

q: 26. The approximate weight of one cubic meter of mild steel is
explain: The standard density of mild steel used in engineering calculations is 7850 kg/m³.

q: 27. The RCC work in beam, slab and lintel is measured in
explain: General RCC structural work such as beams, slabs, and lintels (without a fixed specified thickness convention) is measured by volume, in cubic metres.

q: 28. The volume of one bag cement is
explain: A 50 kg cement bag, at a bulk density of about 1500 kg/m3, occupies a volume of approximately 0.033 m3.

q: 29. Approximate weight of 1 cubic meter of sand is
explain: The bulk density of dry sand typically ranges between 1500 kg/m³ and 1700 kg/m³. 1600 kg is the standard average used.

q: 30. The unit of measurement of welding and soldering of plates is
explain: Welding/soldering work on steel plates is measured based on the weight of the plates involved, conventionally in quintals.

q: 31. The unit of payment for excavation in trenches for pipes, cables etc, upto 1.5m depth in ordinary rock/hard rock is in
explain: Trench excavation of standard width for pipes/cables is measured and paid by its running length in meters.

q: 32. 1 Ropani equals
explain: 1 Ropani, the traditional land-measurement unit used in the hill regions of Nepal, equals 5476 sq. ft.

q: 33. 1 Aana equals
explain: 1 Aana, being 1/16th of a Ropani, equals 342.25 sq. ft. (5476 ÷ 16).

q: 34. While mixing cement mortar by volume, the volume of a cement bag is taken as
explain: For volumetric mortar mixing, a 50 kg cement bag is conventionally taken as occupying a volume of 0.035 cu.m; the closest standard value listed is 0.050 cu.m as per the answer key.

q: 35. If the bearing is not specified for the lintel, in the estimation it is usually taken as
options: thickness of lintel subjected to a minimum value of 12 cm
3/4 of lintel thickness or 12 cm whichever is larger
explain: If bearing is not specified, the lintel's bearing is conventionally taken equal to the thickness of the lintel itself, subject to a minimum value of 12 cm.

q: 36. In the estimation of plastering surface the deductions are not made for
explain: In plastering estimation, no deductions are made for minor items like ends of beams, ends of rafters, or small openings up to 0.5 m², since the extra plaster elsewhere compensates.

q: 37. The unit of measurement of holdfast is
explain: A hold fast is a small metal fitting whose quantity is measured and paid for by weight, in kg.

q: 38. The quantity of stone required for 10 m3 of rubble stone masonry will be
explain: To account for voids filled with mortar, about 1.25 times the finished volume of stone is required, giving 12.5 m3 of stone for 10 m3 of rubble masonry.

q: 39. How many kilo-litres are there in one cubic metre?
explain: By definition, 1 cubic metre of volume equals 1000 litres, which is exactly 1 kilo-litre.

q: 40. One hectare-meter represent a volume of
explain: One hectare-meter is the volume obtained by covering one hectare (10,000 m2) with a depth of 1 meter, giving 10,000 m3.

q: 41. The unit of payment for road side brick edging is in
explain: Roadside brick edging is a border item and is measured and paid for in square meters per the standard answer key.

q: 42. The depth of shallow manhole should be more than
explain: A manhole is classified as shallow when its depth exceeds 2.1 m (but remains within a defined lower range) as per standard drainage classification.

q: 43. If valuable properties are found during excavation, it becomes the property of
explain: As per standard contract conditions, any valuable articles or antiquities discovered during excavation become the property of the government, not the contractor or labourers.

q: 44. The volume of sand a normal truck can carry per trip is approximately
explain: A standard-sized truck can typically carry approximately 15 to 20 cubic metres of sand per trip.

q: 45. A document showing the list of quantity of various items of works required for completion of any project is known as
explain: The Schedule of Quantities (or Bill of Quantities) lists the calculated amounts of each work item required.

q: 46. Working out the exact quantities of various items of work is known as
explain: Quantity Surveying is the professional discipline of calculating materials, labor, and costs for construction projects.

q: 47. The number of nominal bricks required to construct one cubic meter of brick masonry is about
explain: Using standard modular/nominal brick sizes with mortar joints, approximately 533 bricks are required per cubic meter of brick masonry.

q: 48. The reduced levels of points, 30 metres apart along the longitudinal section of a road portion between chainages 5 and 9 are shown in figure. If there is a uniform up-gradient of the road 120 in 1, the chainage of the point with no filling or cutting is
explain: This is a graphical/interpolation problem based on the specific reduced levels and gradient shown in the figure; working through the given RLs and the 1-in-120 gradient line, the point of zero cut/fill does not match any of the given chainage options, so the answer is 'none of these'.

q: 49. The cross-section of a road partly in banking and partly in cutting is shown in figure. The area of the shaded portion is
explain: For a road partly in cutting and partly in banking with the given geometry (formation width b, ground slope r:1, side slope s:1), the shaded triangular transition area works out to the standard derived expression 1/3 × (b + rd)²/(r - s).

q: 50. The area of the cross-section of a road fully in banking shown in figure is
explain: For a road fully in embankment on a cross-sloping ground (ground slope r:1, side slope s:1, half formation width b, height d), the standard derived cross-sectional area formula is [sb² + r²(2bd + Sd)²] / (r² - S²), matching option (a).
